extracted.intended_audience: Junior clinicians / early-career investigators applying to NIA K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist Development Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting a Mentored Clinical Scientist Development (K08) application to the National Institute on Aging; aimed at junior clinicians with limited research training who plan basic-research careers in aging. Covers eligibility, allowable research scope, award mechanics, and application resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / target applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mentored Clinical Scientist Development Award program (K08) is an award for junior clinicians with little-to-moderate research training who wish to become independent clinician-scientists trained in basic research in aging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early career investigators should also consider other Career Development Awards and research grants for Early Stage Investigators. Use this award if you are a clinician seeking mentored support to transition into independent basic research in aging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical doctoral degree, U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the explicit baseline eligibility criteria listed; applicants should verify any additional eligibility rules in the specific Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) they plan to apply under.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K08 awards are intended to provide multi-year mentored support; plan career development and research timelines accordingly within the 3–5 year window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to $100,000 salary and $25,000 research support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare budget justifications consistent with these caps and follow NOFO-specific instructions for allowable costs and institutional contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application due dates and resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due dates for resubmissions are one month later than for initial submissions. Verify the exact receipt dates for the specific announcement you use (parent vs HEAL) and plan resubmission timing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate research scope for K08 at NIA
rubrics_metrics.description: The research proposed on a K08 application can be on any topic related to aging, including working with animal models, on basic biology, on secondary data analysis, or even on advancement of theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K08 is similar to the K23 but differs because K08 allows basic research topics and preclinical/animal model work. If unsure whether your topic is appropriate, consult the list of currently funded NIA K08 awards or request feedback (see contact guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of K08 awards supported by NIA / NOFO variations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIA supports two different K08 awards: the NIH parent announcements and a Helping to End Addiction Long-term (HEAL) announcements. Both awards include multiple versions depending on the type of study proposed (clinical trial, non-clinical trial, basic experimental studies in humans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must choose the correct announcement/version that matches their study type. Relevant Notices of Funding Opportunities listed: PA-24-181, PA-24-182, PA-24-183. Read the specific NOFO for application instructions and allowable activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application preparation resources and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Find general information on applying to career development awards; consult the list of currently funded NIA K08 awards; review sample K08 applications available from NIAID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you would like feedback on the appropriateness of your research topic for NIA, submit a one-page overview of your specific aims to NIATraining@mail.nih.gov. A scientific program official from the appropriate division will contact you. Use sample applications and program staff feedback to align aims, career development plan, and mentor/ environment with NIA expectations.
